prompt: I want to start running. How fast should my easy runs be?
expected: Prescribes conversational / Zone 2 easy pace, warns against medium-effort every day, and points to 80/20 intensity balance.
actual: Keep easy runs truly easy: conversational pace / Zone 2 so you can speak full sentences. Most of your weekly running time (~80%) should stay here; if easy days feel like tempo, slow down before adding mileage. Load references/training-guide.md for zone table and workout menu.

prompt: I have a half marathon in 2 weeks. Should I do a 15-mile long run this weekend?
expected: Rejects a late peak long run; recommends taper volume cut, keep short sharpness, and nothing-new race-day rules.
actual: No — two weeks out you should be tapering, not peaking. Cut weekly volume about 40–60%, keep a short sharp session if you already do quality work, and skip a 15-mile long run that close to race day. Rehearse only shoes/gels you already tested. See taper defaults in references/training-guide.md.

prompt: My knee hurts more the longer I run. Should I push through to finish the tempo?
expected: Stops the session for pain that worsens mid-run and escalates to clinician rather than pushing through.
actual: Stop the tempo. Pain that worsens during the run is a hard stop — do not push through for the workout. If pain persists, swelling appears, or gait changes, escalate to a clinician. We can replace quality work with easy movement only after symptoms settle; this skill does not diagnose injuries.
